newsitem.title: DENMARK: Swedes find letter-bombs destined for London.
newsitem.headline: Swedes find letter-bombs destined for London.

text.p: Danish police on Saturday arrested seven members of an extreme right-wing group they said planned to send letter bombs to addresses in London, but said three bombs intercepted in Sweden contained only detonators.

A Danish policeman was shot and wounded during one of three raids following a tipoff from an international police intelligence unit in Germany and the interception of the three devices in Sweden, Copenhagen police said.

Detective Commander Per Larsen told a news conference that Saturday's raids, on two locations in the capital and a house in the seaside village of Nivaa, 20 km (eight miles) to the north, had uncovered explosives and detonators.
Three devices made in Nivaa were intercepted by Swedish police in the port city of Malmo, a short ferry trip from Copenhagen, where the bombers had taken them for posting, he added.
"They were disguised as video tapes and were to be sent to addresses in London. I will not at this point say anything about the intended recipients," Larsen said.
Police said initially that the devices were live bombs but an examination by Swedish police later showed that they contained only priming charges.

"The material packed around the detonators proved not to explosive, as was first thought, but the detonators themselves are dangerous enough and could easily cost a couple of fingers," Copenhagen murder squad chief Kurt Jensen told the Danish news agency Ritzau.

"First indications are that an extreme right-wing group here in Denmark is being controlled from abroad, with the intention of hitting international targets. We are still in full swing with our searches and would not rule out further arrests," Jensen told the news conference earlier.
Police said Thomas Derry Nakaba, Danish-born despite his name, shot a policeman in the groin with a pistol as police broke into the Nivaa house.
"The shot passed through a door, so luckily much of its force was reduced before it hit," Jensen said.

"Nakaba said afterwards that he did not know it was police breaking in but thought it was leftist elements. When he realised that it was the police he gave himself up immediately," he said, adding that the wounded man was recovering well after surgery.
In addition to 26-year-old Nakaba, Danish police arrested five men and a woman, all aged between 20 and 22, they said.
